title: Maj. Silas Harlan
summary: Maj. Silas Harlan built Harlan’s Station south of Harrodsburg in 1778 and was killed leading an advance party at Blue Licks on August 19, 1782.
bodyMarkdown:
Silas Harlan was a Virginia-born frontier soldier who came to Kentucky in its earliest years of settlement and died leading the advance at the Battle of Blue Licks. The [Kentucky Historical Society marker for Harlan County](https://history.ky.gov/markers/county-named-1819) gives his birth year as 1752. Another account of [Silas Harlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silas_Harlan) gives March 17, 1753.

## Early Kentucky

Harlan came to Kentucky in 1774 with James Harrod's party, which laid out the settlement at [Harrodsburg](https://grokipedia.com/page/Harrodsburg,_Kentucky). In 1776 he supported making Kentucky a county of Virginia rather than accepting the claims of Richard Henderson's Transylvania Company. In January 1777 he was one of about thirty men Harrod raised to bring five hundred pounds of gunpowder from Three Islands, in present-day Lewis County, to the Kentucky stations.

In 1778 Harlan built a station with his uncle Jacob and brother James. The sources disagree on where it stood. The KHS marker places it 7 miles south of Harrodsburg on the Salt River. It stood near Danville, about seven miles above Harrodsburg.

## Soldier and scout

Harlan served under [George Rogers Clark](/stories/george-rogers-clark/) in the 1779 phase of the [Illinois campaign](https://grokipedia.com/page/Illinois_campaign), where he commanded the spies, or scouts. He was a captain on John Bowman's 1779 raid on the Shawnee town of Chillicothe. In 1780 he helped at Fort Jefferson, Clark's post near the Mississippi River.

Clark valued him highly. The KHS marker quotes Clark: "He was one of bravest soldiers that ever fought by my side." Another account gives the quote in slightly different words.

## Blue Licks

On August 19, 1782, Kentucky militia caught up with a force of British rangers and Shawnee, Delaware and Wyandot warriors at the Lower Blue Licks on the Licking River. The [Grokipedia entry on the battle](https://grokipedia.com/page/Battle_of_Blue_Licks) describes the ambush that followed. Harlan, then a major, led the advance and was killed. He was buried at the battlefield. The battle is told in [Battle of Blue Licks](/stories/battle-of-blue-licks/).

## Family legacy

His fiancée, Sarah Caldwell, later married his brother James. Through that marriage she became the grandmother of John Marshall Harlan, who served on the U.S. Supreme Court.

## Kentucky today

The Kentucky legislature created Harlan County in 1819 and named it for him. The [Grokipedia entry on Harlan County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Harlan_County,_Kentucky) notes that it was formed mainly from Knox County. He is remembered at the Blue Licks battlefield, where he was buried, and through the mountain county that carries his name.
